summary: pino-std ships obfuscated dynamic-code-execution payload under a typosquat of pino-std-serializers
details: The package name resembles the legitimate pino-std-serializers and the tarball reproduces that project's source files, README, and author metadata nearly verbatim. In addition, it ships an undocumented file lib/contract.js that is not referenced from index.js, the README, or any lifecycle script. contract.js reconstructs a function body from a character-shuffled/char-code-substituted string and executes it via the Function constructor reached indirectly through a prototype's constructor property (ype.constructor). The same file stashes the Node require function into a global variable before invoking the reconstructed code, which lets the hidden payload load arbitrary built-in and installed modules once reached. The combination of a lookalike package name, verbatim copying of an upstream project to serve as cover, an added undocumented file that runtime-assembles and executes opaque code, and a global-require stash is the shape of a dormant/second-stage loader rather than legitimate functionality. The payload is not invoked from the package's main entry or from a lifecycle hook, so installing or requiring pino-std does not auto-detonate it in a default npm install; execution requires the file to be reached by a consumer or a later-added import.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
